meta.title: Grasp
meta.description: See how a system corrects itself — and why you should believe it: a cybernetics graph with relation annotations, deterministic experiments, and coding-agent task contracts, with personal evidence attached to the same node ids.

messages.loop.coach.gap.adaptation-failure.firstA: Change the rule, not the force: write down which rule you will change given the same action already failed (e.g. stop raising the retry cap and switch strategy on the first failure).
messages.loop.coach.gap.adaptation-failure.label: Adaptation failure
messages.loop.coach.gap.authority-gap.firstAction: Find the smallest lever you truly control and state it as a concrete action (e.g. run one check before every merge), not as "make everyone more responsible". If there is none, build the loop only for the part you own.
messages.loop.coach.gap.authority-gap.label: No lever
messages.loop.coach.gap.drift.firstAction: Fix the measurement before adding memory: check the number still tracks the goal (e.g. switch from pass rate back to rollback count), then add a cumulative term so a small persistent error still triggers action.
messages.loop.coach.gap.drift.label: Drifting
messages.loop.coach.gap.late-measurement.firstAct: Shorten the loop once: split a large change into a step you can observe alone, or move the check earlier (e.g. from the day after release to ten minutes before merge). If you cannot shorten it, make the observation window longer than the delay.
messages.loop.coach.gap.late-measurement.label: Feedback too late
messages.loop.coach.gap.missing-counter-signal.fi: Write one observation that would change your mind and can be checked against data (e.g. "if the retry rate does not drop by ten percent within a week, the model is not the problem").
messages.loop.coach.gap.oscillating.firstAction: Lower the gain first, then look at delay: halve each adjustment and make the observation window longer than one full swing (e.g. one day to three). If it still oscillates, examine the delay between action and result.
messages.loop.coach.gap.oscillating.label: Oscillating
messages.loop.coach.gap.proxy.firstAction: Add a second metric independent of the current one (e.g. count rollbacks as well as passing tests), and write down when the two would conflict and which one wins then.
messages.loop.coach.gap.proxy.label: Proxy as goal
messages.loop.coach.gap.saturated.firstAction: You are at the limit; pushing harder only makes it worse. Lower the gain one notch (e.g. retries from three to one) or switch action channel, then wait a full feedback cycle before judging.
messages.loop.coach.gap.saturated.label: Lever saturated
messages.loop.coach.gap.unclear-goal.firstAction: Rewrite the goal as one sentence that can be judged true or false: which quantity, what value, within what time window. Then add one sentence on what you do not control and keep it as the boundary. If no quantity comes out, start with a count you can tally.
messages.loop.coach.gap.unclear-goal.label: Goal unclear
messages.loop.coach.gap.unmeasured.firstAction: Define one minimal measurement: a single number or one log line, plus how often you read it (e.g. test pass rate before every merge). Skip accuracy for now; tomorrow you must be able to read the same number again.
messages.loop.coach.gap.unmeasured.label: No measurement
messages.loop.coach.question.action.hint: List concrete levers: permissions, tools, time, people, release switches. Write down what you cannot change — that becomes your boundary.
messages.loop.coach.question.action.title: What can you change directly, and what can't you?
messages.loop.coach.question.action.unknown: If no lever is available, shrink the scope: build the loop around the part you own in this system rather than the whole thing.
messages.loop.coach.question.delay.hint: Give an order of magnitude: minutes, hours, days. Write 'unknown' if unsure — that itself is gap information.
messages.loop.coach.question.delay.title: How long from your action to a visible result?
messages.loop.coach.question.delay.unknown: If the delay is unknown, make the check interval longer: wait at least as long as feels 'enough' before judging, and record the wait in the observation window.
messages.loop.coach.question.disturbance.hint: Scope changes, flaky tests, model variance, upstream dependencies, concurrency, human attention — all count.
messages.loop.coach.question.disturbance.title: Which outside changes push it off target?
messages.loop.coach.question.disturbance.unknown: Leaving it blank is fine, but put 'observe for one day' as your next action; disturbances often only show up in hindsight.
messages.loop.coach.question.goal.hint: Aim for a quantity or state that can be judged, e.g. "tests pass with no regressions before each commit".
messages.loop.coach.question.goal.title: What are you trying to keep stable or make better?
messages.loop.coach.question.goal.unknown: If no quantity comes to mind, write what you do not want it to become; it is recorded as "goal unclear" and we rewrite it into a checkable sentence next.
messages.loop.coach.question.hypothesis.hint: Both parts are required: a claim about why, and an observation that would refute it.
messages.loop.coach.question.hypothesis.title: What is your current explanation — and what would change your mind?
messages.loop.coach.question.hypothesis.unknown: A claim alone can still create the card; record 'missing a falsifying observation' as a gap and add it next time.
messages.loop.coach.question.measurement.hint: Tests, logs, reviews, user feedback and gut feeling all count — but state what you look at and how often.
messages.loop.coach.question.measurement.title: How do you currently know whether it is good or bad?
messages.loop.coach.question.measurement.unknown: "No measurement" is fine to admit: borrow one number that already exists (test result, review note, rollback log) and read it once a day — that beats guessing.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.example: e.g. I can change the prompt checklist and the retry cap; I cannot change model weights or the eval set.
e.g. Two to three turns to see whether a prompt change is stable; CI takes about 10 minutes.
e.g. The same commit fails intermittently in CI; after long sessions the model stops following the format.
e.g. In a task of at most 20 turns, the first test run after the change passes with no regressions.
e.g. Failures cluster late in the session, so I suspect context pressure; if the first five turns fail just as often, the explanation fails.
e.g. Per task, read failed tool calls over total turns, and the turn at which tests first pass.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.ac: List what you can change — prompt, tool set, retry cap, context budget — and what you cannot: model weights, upstream APIs.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.de: From a prompt change to a visible difference is usually one to several turns; state how many you will wait before judging.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.di: Typical disturbances: flaky tests, model variance, truncated context, upstream changes, concurrent jobs.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.go: Formulate it as the quantity the agent must hold within one task (pass rate, turns, time-to-green), plus a time window.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.hy: Make the claim about a mechanism (e.g. failures come from context overflow) and add one observation that would refute it.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.hint.me: Prefer numbers the session already has: test results, tool failure and retry counts, time to first success.
messages.loop.coach.template.coding-agent.label: Coding agent
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.act: e.g. I can leave my phone in another room and lower practice difficulty one notch; I cannot reduce this week's workload.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.del: e.g. Four weeks to know whether the practice works; in between I only count sessions, not results.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.dis: e.g. Meetings run late on Thursday; chores fill the weekend.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.goa: e.g. For four straight weeks, at least three 40-minute deliberate-practice sessions per week.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.hyp: e.g. Plateaus come from practice being too hard; if a lower difficulty does not remove them, suspect the method.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.example.mea: e.g. One line after each session — what I practiced and where I got stuck — counted every Sunday.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.action: List changes you can make alone — time blocks, environment, practice difficulty — and note what is externally constrained.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.delay: From practice to a visible effect usually takes weeks; set a check point a few weeks out.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.distur: Typical disturbances: poor sleep, overtime, social interruptions, information overload.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.goal: Aim at the state or capability you want to sustain: sessions per week, focus streak, error rate.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.hypoth: The claim must distinguish "too little practice" from "wrong practice", with an observation that tells them apart.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.hint.measur: Use traces you already leave — study log, commit history, focus timer — not after-the-fact memory.
messages.loop.coach.template.personal.label: Personal learning
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.acti: e.g. I can cut scope and use a canary switch; I cannot decide budget or the launch date.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.dela: e.g. Retention shifts show 3—7 days after release; two weeks to judge whether to roll back.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.dist: e.g. A big customer adds a last-minute requirement; the payment API changes.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.goal: e.g. Two consecutive releases with no rollback and no P1 incident within 24 hours.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.hypo: e.g. Acceptance disputes come from vague criteria; if disputes persist once criteria are written up front, the requirement itself is unclear.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.example.meas: e.g. Read the rollback log and acceptance notes after each release, summarized every Friday.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.action: State what you decide — scope cuts, release switch, acceptance bar — and what needs someone else to approve.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.delay: From release to a visible user response is usually days to two weeks; judgments inside that window do not count.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.disturb: Typical disturbances: mid-flight scope changes, upstream delays, incidents, key people away.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.goal: Pick an outward promise as the quantity: rollbacks, release cadence, first-pass acceptance rate.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.hypothe: The claim must separate "wrong requirement" from "wrong execution", plus one observation that tells them apart.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.hint.measure: Use existing release records and review outcomes, not a new dashboard; state how often you read them.
messages.loop.coach.template.product.label: Product / project
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.action: e.g. I can require that whoever changes scope writes the acceptance, and fix a Wednesday sync; I cannot change the company approval flow.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.delay: e.g. About three weeks after changing the sync format to see whether rework drops.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.disturb: e.g. Quarter-end support for another project; two core members on leave at once.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.goal: e.g. At most two reworks per iteration, each with a recorded cause.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.hypothe: e.g. Rework comes from vague acceptance; if rework persists once acceptance is written, look at scheduling instead.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.example.measure: e.g. Weekly, read task status changes and rework logs; the standup only looks at these two.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.action: Name the mechanisms you can change: who signs off at which checkpoint, where information lives; list processes you cannot change.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.delay: From a collaboration change to changed behavior usually takes one iteration or more; no change in a short window is expected.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.disturbanc: Typical disturbances: turnover, priority interrupts, cross-team dependencies, verbal-only information.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.goal: Aim at the collaboration outcome the team must hold: on-time delivery, rework count, decision-to-execution lag.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.hypothesis: Point the claim at a coordination failure type — no owner, no information, no decision point — and add an observation that distinguishes them.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.hint.measuremen: Use existing traces — meeting notes, task status, rework logs — not new reporting forms.
messages.loop.coach.template.team.label: Team collaboration
